style: Hand-inked comic print style for a game sprite source: a BOLD black brush-ink outer outline on every figure (thick enough to survive being drawn small), confident inner ink lines, flat fills with 2-3 value steps, light cross-hatching in the shadows, a subtle riso print grain. Every figure is isolated on a FLAT SOLID #00B140 chroma-green background that fills the whole image: no ground plane, no floor, no cast shadow, no scenery, no frame, no gradient. Colour law: teal-cyan appears ONLY on the ghosts (they are souls); police blue never; blood red never; vermilion-orange only on the hero's hazard collar, the King's cape and danger marks. Original design. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no UI.

jobs.name: rivet_55
jobs.prompt: GAME VIEW SHEET of RIVET, the slim robot hero. Image 1 is his identity (keep exactly: the rounded tan riveted helmet with the dark horizontal visor slot and the bolt on top, the light warm-tan riveted plating, the vermilion-and-black hazard-striped neck collar). Image 2 is his body and proportions (slim, lanky factory robot, claw hands, a welding-torch left forearm). Image 3 shows how his head already reads in the game at five facings. CAMERA: a fixed game camera looking DOWN at 55 degrees below the horizon: a high three-quarter view, halfway between a side view and a straight-down top view. You see the top of the helmet and the shoulders AND the visor face and the chest; the legs and feet are foreshortened and shorter in frame. Every drawing on the sheet uses this same camera. LAYOUT: TOP ROW: Rivet standing, five times, the SAME size, feet on one shared baseline, evenly spaced, turning on the spot: (1) facing the camera, (2) turned three-quarter to the right toward the camera, (3) side profile facing right, (4) turned three-quarter to the right away from the camera, (5) back to the camera. BOTTOM ROW, larger: three action poses from the same 55-degree camera for close combat: (a) a claw jab lunging toward the camera-right, (b) firing a compact pistol held in the right claw, (c) a hit reaction recoiling back. Higher detail than a turnaround: rivet heads, panel seams, scuffs, wear, readable at close zoom, but a clean silhouette first.

jobs.name: king_55
jobs.prompt: BOSS GAME VIEW SHEET of the KING, Act 1's boss, ON FOOT. Image 1 is his design (keep his squat hydraulic press-robot body, the two flat gold press-plate arms, the jewelled gold crown over a dented tin crown, the vermilion cape lined with thick white ermine fur, the shoulder megaphone, the fat gold chains with a gem medallion). BOSS PALETTE: use a WIDER, RICHER palette than the street cast: burnished gold leaf with highlights, deep plum velvet, ivory ermine with black tail tips, polished steel, gem colours (amethyst, emerald), brass; more surface detail (engraving, rivets, chain links, fur texture) because players see him close in melee. CAMERA: a fixed game camera looking DOWN at 55 degrees below the horizon: a high three-quarter view, halfway between a side view and a straight-down top view; you see the crown and shoulders AND the face, chest chains and medallion; legs foreshortened. Every drawing uses this camera. LAYOUT: TOP ROW: the King five times, the same size, on one shared baseline, turning on the spot: facing the camera, three-quarter right toward the camera, side profile facing right, three-quarter right away from the camera (the cape fills the back), back to the camera. BOTTOM ROW, larger: two attack poses from the same camera: (a) the press slam, both gold plates raised overhead, cape flaring, (b) the charge, head down, cape streaming behind.
